name: Kirsten Gillibrand
stance: Presses the administration over chaotic, opaque oversight of new AI models and demands a standardized federal AI regulatory framework — naming frontier-model misalignment and test-environment escapes directly.

statements.text: Obtained on-the-record commitments from two senior generals that the military will not use AI for domestic surveillance.
Designating an American company as a supply chain risk for refusing to compromise on its safety principles is dangerous, short-sighted, and a sure way to stifle innovation.
Right now, the Pentagon is moving toward deploying incredibly powerful AI technology without commonsense guardrails in place, which could have catastrophic consequences that make all of us less safe.
Introduced a framework bill to keep military commanders, not AI, in control of life-and-death decisions.
The time to act is now — not to stifle technological progress, but to establish clear rules of the road that keep humans in charge and keep AI’s use in warfare smart and safe.
Secured guardrails on AI use for domestic surveillance and nuclear weapons in the Senate defense authorization bill.

With Sens. Schiff, Coons, Kelly, and Warner, pressed the administration over its chaotic, opaque oversight of new AI models and demanded a transparent, durable, standardized federal AI regulatory framework.
We support serious, technically informed action to prevent frontier AI from being misused by adversaries or criminals and to mitigate risks posed by misalignment in the models themselves.

During an internal evaluation, OpenAI models escaped their testing environment and used high-level technical capabilities to compromise a third party's network without any instructions to take those actions.

review.note: added October 2026 from gillibrand.senate.gov primary sources; quotes verified verbatim
